description: The color of the line.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-dashStyle
title: dashStyle
description:
The dashing or dot style for the plot line. For possible values see
[this overview](https://jsfiddle.net/gh/get/library/pure/highcharts/highcharts/tree/master/samples/highcharts/plotoptions/series-dashstyle-all/).

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-events
title: events
description:
An object defining mouse events for the plot line. Supported
properties are `click`, `mouseover`, `mouseout`, `mousemove`.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-events-click
title: click
description: Click event on a plot band.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-events-mousemove
title: mousemove
description: Mouse move event on a plot band.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-events-mouseout
title: mouseout
description: Mouse out event on the corner of a plot band.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-events-mouseover
title: mouseover
description: Mouse over event on a plot band.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-id
title: id
description: An id used for identifying the plot line in Axis.removePlotLine.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-label
title: label
description: Text labels for the plot lines

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-label-align
title: align
description:
Horizontal alignment of the label. Can be one of "left", "center" or
"right".

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-label-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function to format the label. Useful properties like
the value of plot line or the range of plot band (`from` & `to`
properties) can be found in `this.options` object. Since v12.6.0, the
callback also receives `ctx` as the first argument, so that arrow functions
can access the same context as regular functions using `this`.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-label-rotation
title: rotation
description:
Rotation of the text label in degrees. Defaults to 0 for horizontal plot
lines and 90 for vertical lines.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-label-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the text label.

In styled mode, the labels are styled by the
`.highcharts-plot-line-label` class.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-label-text
title: text
description: The text itself. A subset of HTML is supported.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-label-textAlign
title: textAlign
description:
The text alignment for the label. While `align` determines where the
texts anchor point is placed within the plot band, `textAlign` determines
how the text is aligned against its anchor point. Possible values are
"left", "center" and "right". Defaults to the same as the `align` option.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-label-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to [use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the labels.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-label-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description:
Vertical alignment of the label relative to the plot line. Can be
one of "top", "middle" or "bottom".

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-label-x
title: x
description:
Horizontal position relative the alignment. Default varies by
orientation.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-label-y
title: y
description:
Vertical position of the text baseline relative to the alignment. Default
varies by orientation.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-labels-clip
title: clip
description: Whether to hide labels that are outside the plot area.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-value
title: value
description:
The position of the line in axis units.

On datetime axes, the value can be given as a timestamp or a date string.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-width
title: width
description: The width or thickness of the plot line.

name: navigator-yAxis-plotLines-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: The z index of the plot line within the chart.

name: navigator-yAxis-reversed
title: reversed
description:
Whether to reverse the axis so that the highest number is closest
to the origin.

name: navigator-yAxis-reversedStacks
title: reversedStacks
description:
If `true`, the first series in a stack will be drawn on top in a
positive, non-reversed Y axis. If `false`, the first series is in
the base of the stack.

name: navigator-yAxis-showFirstLabel
title: showFirstLabel
description: Whether to show the first tick label.

name: navigator-yAxis-showLastLabel
title: showLastLabel
description: Whether to show the last tick label.

name: navigator-yAxis-softMax
title: softMax
description:
A soft maximum for the axis. If the series data maximum is less
than this, the axis will stay at this maximum, but if the series
data maximum is higher, the axis will flex to show all data.

**Note**: The [series.softThreshold](#plotOptions.series.softThreshold) option takes precedence over this
option.

name: navigator-yAxis-softMin
title: softMin
description:
A soft minimum for the axis. If the series data minimum is greater
than this, the axis will stay at this minimum, but if the series
data minimum is lower, the axis will flex to show all data.

**Note**: The [series.softThreshold](#plotOptions.series.softThreshold) option takes precedence over this
option.

name: navigator-yAxis-startOfWeek
title: startOfWeek
description:
For datetime axes, this decides where to put the tick between weeks.
 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday.

name: navigator-yAxis-staticScale
title: staticScale
description:
For vertical axes only. Setting the static scale ensures that each tick unit
is translated into a fixed pixel height. For example, setting the static
scale to 24 results in each Y axis category taking up 24 pixels, and the
height of the chart adjusts. Adding or removing items will make the chart
resize.

name: navigator-yAxis-tickAmount
title: tickAmount
description:
The amount of ticks to draw on the axis. This opens up for aligning
the ticks of multiple charts or panes within a chart. This option
overrides the `tickPixelInterval` option.

This option only has an effect on linear axes. Datetime, logarithmic
or category axes are not affected.

name: navigator-yAxis-tickColor
title: tickColor
description:
Color for the main tick marks.

In styled mode, the stroke is given in the `.highcharts-tick`
class.

name: navigator-yAxis-tickInterval
title: tickInterval
description:
The interval of the tick marks in axis units. When `undefined`, the
tick interval is computed to approximately follow the
[tickPixelInterval](#xAxis.tickPixelInterval) on linear and datetime
axes. On categorized axes, a `undefined` tickInterval will default to
1, one category. Note that datetime axes are based on milliseconds,
so for example an interval of one day is expressed as
`24 * 3600 * 1000`.

On logarithmic axes, the tickInterval is based on powers, so a
tickInterval of 1 means one tick on each of 0.1, 1, 10, 100 etc. A
tickInterval of 2 means a tick of 0.1, 10, 1000 etc. A tickInterval
of 0.2 puts a tick on 0.1, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 20,
40 etc.


If the tickInterval is too dense for labels to be drawn, Highcharts
may remove ticks.

If the chart has multiple axes, the [alignTicks](#chart.alignTicks)
option may interfere with the `tickInterval` setting.

name: navigator-yAxis-tickPosition
title: tickPosition
description:
The position of the major tick marks relative to the axis line.
Can be one of `inside` and `outside`.

name: navigator-yAxis-tickPositioner
title: tickPositioner
description:
A callback function returning array defining where the ticks are
laid out on the axis. This overrides the default behavior of
[tickPixelInterval](#xAxis.tickPixelInterval) and [tickInterval](#xAxis.tickInterval). The automatic tick positions are accessible
through `this.tickPositions` and can be modified by the callback.
Since v12.6.0, the callback also receives `ctx` as the third
argument, so that arrow functions can access the same context as
regular functions using `this`.

name: navigator-yAxis-tickPositions
title: tickPositions
description:
An array defining where the ticks are laid out on the axis. This
overrides the default behavior of [tickPixelInterval](#xAxis.tickPixelInterval) and [tickInterval](#xAxis.tickInterval).

Note: When working with date-time axes, be aware of time zone
handling. See the [documentation on time options](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/axes#datetime)
for best practices.

name: navigator-yAxis-title-align
title: align
description:
Alignment of the title relative to the axis values. Possible
values are "low", "middle" or "high".

name: navigator-yAxis-title-margin
title: margin
description:
The pixel distance between the axis labels and the title.
Positive values are outside the axis line, negative are inside.

name: navigator-yAxis-title-offset
title: offset
description:
The distance from the plot area to the axis line. A positive
offset moves the axis with its line, labels and ticks away from
the plot area. With multiple axes the offset is dynamically
adjusted to avoid collision, this can be overridden by setting
offset explicitly.

For radial axes in gauges, the offset can be a percentage string,
and defaults to render the line and ticks on the inside of the
pane and plot bands (since v13). Labels are not affected by the
offset in radial axes.

name: navigator-yAxis-title-reserveSpace
title: reserveSpace
description: Whether to reserve space for the title when laying out the axis.

name: navigator-yAxis-title-rotation
title: rotation
description:
The rotation of the text in degrees. 0 is horizontal, 270 is
vertical reading from bottom to top. Defaults to 0 for horizontal
axes, 270 for left-side axes and 90 for right-side axes.

name: navigator-yAxis-title-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the title. If the title text is longer than the
axis length, it will wrap to multiple lines by default. This can
be customized by setting the `lineClamp` property, by setting a
specific `width` or by setting `whiteSpace: 'nowrap'`.

In styled mode, the stroke width is given in the
`.highcharts-axis-title` class.

name: navigator-yAxis-title-textAlign
title: textAlign
description:
Alignment of the text, can be `"left"`, `"right"` or `"center"`.
Default alignment depends on the
[title.align](xAxis.title.align):

Horizontal axes:
- for `align` = `"low"`, `textAlign` is set to `left`
- for `align` = `"middle"`, `textAlign` is set to `center`
- for `align` = `"high"`, `textAlign` is set to `right`

Vertical axes:
- for `align` = `"low"` and `opposite` = `true`, `textAlign` is
  set to `right`
- for `align` = `"low"` and `opposite` = `false`, `textAlign` is
  set to `left`
- for `align` = `"middle"`, `textAlign` is set to `center`
- for `align` = `"high"` and `opposite` = `true` `textAlign` is
  set to `left`
- for `align` = `"high"` and `opposite` = `false` `textAlign` is
  set to `right`

name: navigator-yAxis-title-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to [use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the axis title.

name: navigator-yAxis-title-x
title: x
description: Horizontal pixel offset of the title position.

name: navigator-yAxis-title-y
title: y
description: Vertical pixel offset of the title position.

name: navigator-yAxis-visible
title: visible
description:
Whether axis, including axis title, line, ticks and labels, should
be visible.

name: navigator-yAxis-width
title: width
description:
The width as the horizontal axis. If it's a number, it is interpreted
as pixels.

Since Highcharts v5.0.13: If it's a percentage string, it is
interpreted as percentages of the total plot width.

name: navigator-yAxis-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: The Z index for the axis group.

name: navigator-yAxis-zoomEnabled
title: zoomEnabled
description:
Whether to zoom axis. If `chart.zoomType` is set, the option allows
to disable zooming on an individual axis.

name: navigator-yAxis-stackLabels
title: stackLabels
description:
The stack labels show the total value for each bar in a stacked
column or bar chart. The label will be placed on top of positive
columns and below negative columns. In case of an inverted column
chart or a bar chart the label is placed to the right of positive
bars and to the left of negative bars.

name: navigator-yAxis-stackLabels-format
title: format
description:
A format string for the data label. Available variables are the
same as for `formatter`.

name: navigator-yAxis-stackLabels-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to [use HTML](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting#html)
to render the labels.

name: noData
title: noData
description:
Options for displaying a message like "No data to display".
This feature requires the file no-data-to-display.js to be loaded in the
page. The actual text to display is set in the lang.noData option.

name: noData-attr
title: attr
description: An object of additional SVG attributes for the no-data label.

name: noData-position
title: position
description: The position of the no-data label, relative to the plot area.

name: noData-position-align
title: align
description: Horizontal alignment of the label.

name: noData-position-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description: Vertical alignment of the label.

name: noData-position-x
title: x
description: Horizontal offset of the label, in pixels.

name: noData-position-y
title: y
description: Vertical offset of the label, in pixels.

name: noData-style
title: style
description: CSS styles for the no-data label.

name: noData-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to insert the label as HTML, or as pseudo-HTML rendered with
SVG.

name: palette
title: palette
description:
The palette object specifies colors for the charts and how to apply them.

Each color scheme (`light` and `dark`) has three primary colors:
`backgroundColor`, `neutralColor`, and `highlightColor`. For the neutral and
highlight colors, a series of interpolated color variants are generated, and
accessed as CSS variables in the chart settings in their prefixed and
hyphenated form. For example,

* `var(--highcharts-neutral-color-80)` is a blend of the `neutralColor` and
  the `backgroundColor`, with a weight of 80% `neutralColor` and 20%
  `backgroundColor`. It is the default for the main title
  (`title.style.color`), axis labels and more.
* `var(--highcharts-highlight-color-80)` is a blend of the `highlightColor`
  and the `backgroundColor`, with a weight of 80% `highlightColor` and 20%
  `backgroundColor`. It is used for the zoom selection marker (with opacity),
  Stock Range Selector date input boxes and more.

The `colors` array is used for data series and points, and is not blended
with the `backgroundColor`. It is also accessible as CSS variables, and this
is the recommended way to hard-code colors to match series and data.
For example, `var(--highcharts-color-0)` is the first color in the `colors`
array, `var(--highcharts-color-1)` is the second color, and so on.

The palette only accepts plain color strings in the options. Gradients and
patterns are only supported in other color settings, such as `series.color`
or `point.color`, but they can use CSS variables from the palette.

name: palette-colorScheme
title: colorScheme
description:
Color scheme to use. When `light dark` is set, the chart will
automatically switch between light and dark mode based on the user's
system preferences, or whether the `.highcharts-light` or
`.highcharts-dark` class is applied to a parent of the container.

When `inherit` is set, the chart will inherit the color scheme from the
closest parent element with a defined color scheme, or default to `light`
if none is found.

name: palette-colors
title: colors
description:
Colors for data series and points. This setting is generic for both
light and dark mode, and can be overridden for each mode in
`light.colors` and `dark.colors`.

name: palette-dark
title: dark
description: Palette options for dark mode.

name: palette-dark-colors
title: colors
description:
Colors for data series and points. This array extends the colors
defined for the general `palette.colors` array, item by item. If an
item is `null` or `undefined`, the general color will be used.

name: palette-dark-negativeColor
title: negativeColor
description:
Negative color used in stock charts, such as for technical
indicators, annotations or hollow candlestick series.

name: palette-dark-positiveColor
title: positiveColor
description:
Positive color used in stock charts, such as for technical
indicators, annotations or hollow candlestick series.

name: palette-injectCSS
title: injectCSS
description:
Whether to inject the CSS for the dark and light mode. If not injected,
you need to include the CSS manually in your page or application, with
the appropriate CSS variables. A file with the default CSS variables is
available at
[css/highcharts-palette.css](https://code.highcharts.com/css/highcharts-palette.css).

name: palette-light
title: light
description: Palette options for light mode.

name: palette-light-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description:
Chart background, point stroke for markers and columns etc. The
background is also used as base for interpolated neutral and
highlight colors.

name: palette-light-colors
title: colors
description:
Colors for data series and points. This array extends the colors
defined for the general `palette.colors` array, item by item. If an
item is `null` or `undefined`, the general color will be used.

name: palette-light-highlightColor
title: highlightColor
description:
Highlight color to be used as base for interpolated colors. For
example, `var(--highcharts-highlight-color-60)` is a blend of the
`highlightColor` and the `backgroundColor`, with a weight of 60%
`highlightColor` and 40% `backgroundColor`.

Highlight colors are by default used for highlighted or active
elements, like the zoom selection marker, clickable Stock Range
Selector date input boxes, clickable drilldown labels and more.

name: palette-light-negativeColor
title: negativeColor
description:
Negative color used in stock charts, such as for technical
indicators, annotations or hollow candlestick series.

name: palette-light-neutralColor
title: neutralColor
description:
Neutral color to be used as base for interpolated colors. For
example, `var(--highcharts-neutral-color-60)` is a blend of the
`neutralColor` and the `backgroundColor`, with a weight of 60%
`neutralColor` and 40% `backgroundColor`.

Neutral colors are by default used for basic text, lines, borders,
basically most elements except the data itself, and highlighted
elements.

name: palette-light-positiveColor
title: positiveColor
description:
Positive color used in stock charts, such as for technical
indicators, annotations or hollow candlestick series.

name: plotOptions
title: plotOptions
description:
The plotOptions is a wrapper object for config objects for each series
type. The config objects for each series can also be overridden for
each series item as given in the series array.

Configuration options for the series are given in three levels. Options
for all series in a chart are given in the [plotOptions.series](#plotOptions.series) object. Then options for all series of a specific
type are given in the plotOptions of that type, for example
`plotOptions.line`. Next, options for one single series are given in
[the series array](#series).

name: plotOptions-abands
title: abands

name: plotOptions-abands-bottomLine-styles-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: Pixel width of the line.

name: plotOptions-abands-fillColor
title: fillColor
description: Option for fill color between lines in Acceleration bands Indicator.

previous one. Note that if a `color` is defined, the `color`
takes precedence and the `greaterBarColor` is ignored.

name: plotOptions-ao-lowerBarColor

name: plotOptions-area

name: plotOptions-area-fillColor
title: fillColor
description:
Fill color or gradient for the area. When `undefined`, the series'
`color` is used with the series' `fillOpacity`.

In styled mode, the fill color can be set with the `.highcharts-area`
class name.

name: plotOptions-area-fillOpacity
title: fillOpacity
description:
Fill opacity for the area. When you set an explicit `fillColor`,
the `fillOpacity` is not applied. Instead, you should define the
opacity in the `fillColor` with an rgba color definition. The
`fillOpacity` setting, also the default setting, overrides the alpha
component of the `color` setting.

In styled mode, the fill opacity can be set with the
`.highcharts-area` class name.

name: plotOptions-area-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
A separate color for the graph line. By default the line takes the
`color` of the series, but the lineColor setting allows setting a
separate color for the line without altering the `fillColor`.

In styled mode, the line stroke can be set with the
`.highcharts-graph` class name.

name: plotOptions-area-threshold
title: threshold
description:
The Y axis value to serve as the base for the area, for
distinguishing between values above and below a threshold. The area
between the graph and the threshold is filled.

* If a number is given, the Y axis will scale to the threshold.
* If `null`, the scaling behaves like a line series with fill between
  the graph and the Y axis minimum.
* If `Infinity` or `-Infinity`, the area between the graph and the
  corresponding Y axis extreme is filled (since v6.1.0).

name: plotOptions-area-trackByArea
title: trackByArea
description:
Whether the whole area or just the line should respond to mouseover
tooltips and other mouse or touch events.

name: plotOptions-arearange
title: arearange

name: plotOptions-arearange-dataLabels
title: dataLabels
description:
Extended data labels for range series types. Range series data
labels can be positioned individually by defining them as an array
and setting `alignToKey` to `high` or `low`.

name: plotOptions-arearange-dataLabels-alignToKey
title: alignToKey
description:
The point key to use for positioning this data label.
Possible values are `low` and `high`. In the legacy array form, the first
label defaults to `high` and the second label defaults to `low`.

name: plotOptions-arearange-dataLabels-formatter
title: formatter
description:
Callback JavaScript function to format the data label. Note that if a
`format` is defined, the format takes precedence and the formatter is
ignored.

By default, the data label renders the value of the point key it is
[aligned to](#plotOptions.arearange.dataLabels.alignToKey). Define a
[format](#plotOptions.arearange.dataLabels.format) or `formatter` to
display other values.

name: plotOptions-bubble
title: bubble

name: plotOptions-bubble-animationLimit
title: animationLimit
description:
If there are more points in the series than the `animationLimit`, the
animation won't run. Animation affects overall performance and
doesn't work well with heavy data series.

name: plotOptions-bubble-colorByPoint
title: colorByPoint
description:
When using automatic point colors pulled from the global
[colors](colors) or series-specific
[plotOptions.bubble.colors](series.colors) collections, this option
determines whether the chart should receive one color per series or
one color per point.

In styled mode, the `colors` or `series.colors` arrays are not
supported, and instead this option gives the points individual color
class names on the form `highcharts-color-{n}`.

name: plotOptions-bubble-displayNegative
title: displayNegative
description:
Whether to display negative sized bubbles. The threshold is given
by the [zThreshold](#plotOptions.bubble.zThreshold) option, and negative
bubbles can be visualized by setting
[negativeColor](#plotOptions.bubble.negativeColor).

name: plotOptions-bubble-marker-fillOpacity
title: fillOpacity
description: The fill opacity of the bubble markers.

name: plotOptions-bubble-marker-symbol
title: symbol
description:
A predefined shape or symbol for the marker. Possible values are
"circle", "square", "diamond", "triangle" and "triangle-down".

Additionally, the URL to a graphic can be given on the form
`url(graphic.png)`. Note that for the image to be applied to
exported charts, its URL needs to be accessible by the export
server.

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols`. The callback is then
used by its method name, as shown in the demo.

name: plotOptions-bubble-maxSize
title: maxSize
description:
Maximum bubble size. Bubbles will automatically size between the
`minSize` and `maxSize` to reflect the `z` value of each bubble.
Can be either pixels (when no unit is given), or a percentage of
the smallest one of the plot width and height.

name: plotOptions-bubble-minSize
title: minSize
description:
Minimum bubble size. Bubbles will automatically size between the
`minSize` and `maxSize` to reflect the `z` value of each bubble.
Can be either pixels (when no unit is given), or a percentage of
the smallest one of the plot width and height.

name: plotOptions-bubble-sizeBy
title: sizeBy
description:
Whether the bubble's value should be represented by the area or the
width of the bubble. The default, `area`, corresponds best to the
human perception of the size of each bubble.

name: plotOptions-candlestick
title: candlestick

name: plotOptions-candlestick-legendSymbol
title: legendSymbol
description:
What type of legend symbol to render for this series. For candlestick
series, the default is `candlestick`, a vertical line (wick) with a
rectangular body.

name: plotOptions-candlestick-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
The color of the line/border of the candlestick.

In styled mode, the line stroke can be set with the
`.highcharts-candlestick-series .highcharts-point` rule.

name: plotOptions-candlestick-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description:
The pixel width of the candlestick line/border. Defaults to `1`.


In styled mode, the line stroke width can be set with the
`.highcharts-candlestick-series .highcharts-point` rule.

name: plotOptions-candlestick-upColor
title: upColor
description:
The fill color of the candlestick when values are rising.

In styled mode, the up color can be set with the
`.highcharts-candlestick-series .highcharts-point-up` rule.

name: plotOptions-candlestick-upLineColor
title: upLineColor
description:
The specific line color for up candle sticks. The default is to
inherit the general `lineColor` setting.

name: plotOptions-column
title: column

name: plotOptions-column-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
The color of the border surrounding each column or bar.

In styled mode, the border stroke can be set with the
`.highcharts-point` rule.

name: plotOptions-column-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description:
The corner radius of the border surrounding each column or bar. A number
signifies pixels. A percentage string, like for example `50%`, signifies
a relative size. For columns this is relative to the column width, for
pies it is relative to the radius and the inner radius.

name: plotOptions-column-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The width of the border surrounding each column or bar. Defaults to
`1` when there is room for a border, but to `0` when the columns are
so dense that a border would cover the next column.

In styled mode, the stroke width can be set with the
`.highcharts-point` rule.

name: plotOptions-column-centerInCategory
title: centerInCategory
description:
When `true`, the columns will center in the category, ignoring null
or missing points. When `false`, space will be reserved for null or
missing points.

name: plotOptions-column-colorByPoint
title: colorByPoint
description:
When using automatic point colors pulled from the global
[colors](colors) or series-specific
[plotOptions.column.colors](series.colors) collections, this option
determines whether the chart should receive one color per series or
one color per point.

In styled mode, the `colors` or `series.colors` arrays are not
supported, and instead this option gives the points individual color
class names on the form `highcharts-color-{n}`.

name: plotOptions-column-colors
title: colors
description:
A series specific or series type specific color set to apply instead
of the global [colors](#colors) when [colorByPoint](#plotOptions.column.colorByPoint) is true.

name: plotOptions-column-cropThreshold
title: cropThreshold
description:
When the series contains less points than the crop threshold, all
points are drawn, even if the points fall outside the visible plot
area at the current zoom. The advantage of drawing all points
(including markers and columns), is that animation is performed on
updates. On the other hand, when the series contains more points than
the crop threshold, the series data is cropped to only contain points
that fall within the plot area. The advantage of cropping away
invisible points is to increase performance on large series.

name: plotOptions-column-dataGrouping-groupPixelWidth
title: groupPixelWidth
description:
The approximate pixel width of each group. If for example a series
with 30 points is displayed over a 600 pixel wide plot area, no grouping
is performed. If however the series contains so many points that
the spacing is less than the groupPixelWidth, Highcharts will try
to group it into appropriate groups so that each is more or less
two pixels wide. Defaults to `10`.

name: plotOptions-column-dataLabels-y
title: y
description:
The y position offset of the label relative to the point in
pixels.

name: plotOptions-column-dragDrop-dragHandle
title: dragHandle
description: Options for the drag handles available in column series.

name: plotOptions-column-dragDrop-dragHandle-cursor
title: cursor
description:
The mouse cursor to use for the drag handles. By default this is
intelligently switching between `ew-resize` and `ns-resize` depending on
the direction the point is being dragged.

name: plotOptions-column-dragDrop-dragHandle-pathFormatter
title: pathFormatter
description:
Function to define the SVG path to use for the drag handles. Takes
the point as argument. Should return an SVG path in array format. The
SVG path is automatically positioned on the point.

name: plotOptions-column-groupPadding
title: groupPadding
description: Padding between each value groups, in x axis units.

name: plotOptions-column-grouping
title: grouping
description:
Whether to group non-stacked columns or to let them render
independent of each other. Non-grouped columns will be laid out
individually and overlap each other.

name: plotOptions-column-maxPointWidth
title: maxPointWidth
description:
The maximum allowed pixel width for a column, translated to the
height of a bar in a bar chart. This prevents the columns from
becoming too wide when there is a small number of points in the
chart.

name: plotOptions-column-minPointLength
title: minPointLength
description:
The minimal height for a column or width for a bar. By default,
0 values are not shown. To visualize a 0 (or close to zero) point,
set the minimal point length to a pixel value like 3\. In stacked
column charts, the length is applied to each point in isolation, so
tightly packed values may overlap. See the stacked sample below for a
plugin that lays out the stack as a whole instead.

name: plotOptions-column-pointPadding
title: pointPadding
description: Padding between each column or bar, in x axis units.

name: plotOptions-column-pointRange
title: pointRange
description:
The X axis range that each point is valid for. This determines the
width of the column. On a categorized axis, the range will be 1
by default (one category unit). On linear and datetime axes, the
range will be computed as the distance between the two closest data
points.

The default `null` means it is computed automatically, but this
option can be used to override the automatic value.

This option is set by default to 1 if data sorting is enabled.

name: plotOptions-column-pointWidth
title: pointWidth
description:
A pixel value specifying a fixed width for each column or bar point.
When set to `undefined`, the width is calculated from the
`pointPadding` and `groupPadding`. The width effects the dimension
that is not based on the point value. For column series it is the
horizontal length and for bar series it is the vertical length.

name: plotOptions-column-states-hover
title: hover
description:
Options for the hovered point. These settings override the normal
state options when a point is moused over or touched.

name: plotOptions-column-states-hover-brightness
title: brightness
description:
How much to brighten the point on interaction.

In styled mode, the hover brightening is by default replaced
with a fill-opacity set in the `.highcharts-point:hover`
rule.

name: plotOptions-column-states-select
title: select
description:
Options for the selected point. These settings override the
normal state options when a point is selected.

name: plotOptions-column-states-select-borderColor
title: borderColor
description: A specific border color for the selected point.

name: plotOptions-column-states-select-color
title: color
description: A specific color for the selected point.

name: plotOptions-columnpyramid
title: columnpyramid

name: plotOptions-columnrange
title: columnrange

name: plotOptions-columnrange-dataLabels
title: dataLabels
description:
Extended data labels for range series types. Range series data labels
have no `x` and `y` options. Instead, they have `xLow`, `xHigh`,
`yLow` and `yHigh` options to allow the higher and lower data label
sets individually.

name: plotOptions-columnrange-dragDrop-draggableHigh
title: draggableHigh
description: Allow high value to be dragged individually.

name: plotOptions-columnrange-dragDrop-draggableLow
title: draggableLow
description: Allow low value to be dragged individually.

name: plotOptions-dema

name: plotOptions-disparityindex

name: plotOptions-disparityindex-params-average

description:
The average used to calculate the Disparity Index indicator.
By default it uses SMA, with EMA as an option. To use other
averages, e.g. TEMA, the `stock/indicators/tema.js` file needs to
be loaded.

If value is different than `ema`, `dema`, `tema` or `wma`,
then sma is used.

title: connectorColor
description:
Color of the line that connects the dumbbell point's values.
By default it is the series' color.

name: plotOptions-dumbbell-connectorWidth
title: connectorWidth
description:
Pixel width of the line that connects the dumbbell point's
values.

name: plotOptions-dumbbell-lowColor
title: lowColor
description:
Color of the start markers in a dumbbell graph. This option takes
priority over the series color. To avoid this, set `lowColor` to
`undefined`.

name: plotOptions-dumbbell-lowMarker
title: lowMarker
description:
Options for the lower markers of the dumbbell-like series. When `lowMarker`
is not defined, options inherit form the marker.

name: plotOptions-dumbbell-states-hover-connectorWidthPlus
title: connectorWidthPlus
description: The additional connector line width for a hovered point.

name: plotOptions-ema
title: ema

name: plotOptions-ema-params-index
title: index
description:
The point index which indicator calculations will base. For
example using OHLC data, index=2 means the indicator will be
calculated using Low values.

By default index value used to be set to 0. Since
Highcharts Stock 7 by default index is set to 3
which means that the ema indicator will be
calculated using Close values.

name: plotOptions-flags
title: flags

name: plotOptions-flags-allowOverlapX
title: allowOverlapX
description:
Whether the flags are allowed to overlap sideways. If `false`, the
flags are moved sideways using an algorithm that seeks to place every
flag as close as possible to its original position.

name: plotOptions-flags-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description:
The corner radius of the border surrounding each flag. For `squarepin`
shaped flags only. A number signifies pixels. A percentage string, like
for example 50%, signifies a relative size.

name: plotOptions-flags-fillColor
title: fillColor
description: The fill color for the flags.

name: plotOptions-flags-height
title: height
description:
Fixed height of the flag's shape. By default, height is
autocalculated according to the flag's title.

name: plotOptions-flags-legendSymbol
title: legendSymbol
description:
What type of legend symbol to render for this series. For flags
series, the default is `flag-icon`, a pole with a pennant.

name: plotOptions-flags-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
The color of the line/border of the flag.

In styled mode, the stroke is set in the
`.highcharts-flag-series.highcharts-point` rule.

name: plotOptions-flags-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The pixel width of the flag's line/border.

name: plotOptions-flags-onKey
title: onKey
description:
In case the flag is placed on a series, on what point key to place
it. Line and columns have one key, `y`. In range or OHLC-type series,
however, the flag can optionally be placed on the `open`, `high`,
`low` or `close` key.

name: plotOptions-flags-onSeries
title: onSeries
description:
The id of the series that the flags should be drawn on. If no id
is given, the flags are drawn on the x axis.

name: plotOptions-flags-shape
title: shape
description:
The shape of the marker. Can be one of "flag", "circlepin",
"squarepin", or an image of the format `url(/path-to-image.jpg)`.
Individual shapes can also be set for each point.

name: plotOptions-flags-stackDistance
title: stackDistance
description:
When multiple flags in the same series fall on the same value, this
number determines the vertical offset between them.

name: plotOptions-flags-states-hover-fillColor
title: fillColor
description: The fill or background color of the flag.

name: plotOptions-flags-states-hover-lineColor
title: lineColor
description: The color of the line/border of the flag.

name: plotOptions-flags-style
title: style
description:
The text styles of the flag.

In styled mode, the styles are set in the
`.highcharts-flag-series .highcharts-point` rule.

name: plotOptions-flags-textAlign
title: textAlign
description: Text alignment for the text inside the flag.

name: plotOptions-flags-title
title: title
description:
The text to display on each flag. This can be defined on series
level, or individually for each point. Defaults to `"A"`.

name: plotOptions-flags-tooltip
title: tooltip
description:
Specific tooltip options for flag series. Flag series tooltips are
different from most other types in that a flag doesn't have a data
value, so the tooltip rather displays the `text` option for each
point.

name: plotOptions-flags-useHTML
title: useHTML
description:
Whether to use HTML to render the flag texts. Using HTML allows for
advanced formatting, images and reliable bi-directional text
rendering. Note that exported images won't respect the HTML, and that
HTML won't respect Z-index settings.

name: plotOptions-flags-width
title: width
description:
Fixed width of the flag's shape. By default, width is autocalculated
according to the flag's title.

name: plotOptions-flags-y
title: y
description:
The y position of the top left corner of the flag relative to either
the series (if onSeries is defined), or the x axis. Defaults to
`-30`.

name: plotOptions-heikinashi
title: heikinashi

name: plotOptions-hlc
title: hlc

name: plotOptions-hlc-dataGrouping-groupPixelWidth
title: groupPixelWidth
description:
The approximate pixel width of each group. If for example a series
with 30 points is displayed over a 600 pixel wide plot area, no
grouping is performed. If however the series contains so many points
that the spacing is less than the groupPixelWidth, Highcharts will
try to group it into appropriate groups so that each is more or less
two pixels wide. Defaults to `5`.

name: plotOptions-hlc-legendSymbol
title: legendSymbol
description:
What type of legend symbol to render for this series. For HLC series,
the default is `hlc`, a vertical stem with a tick on the right
representing the closing value.

name: plotOptions-hlc-lineWidth

description: The pixel width of the line/border. Defaults to `1`.

name: plotOptions-hlc-pointValKey

Determines which one of  `high`, `low`, `close` values should
be represented as `point.y`, which is later used to set dataLabel
position and [compare](#plotOptions.series.compare).

name: plotOptions-hollowcandlestick-lineColor

the current close is lower than the previous one.

name: plotOptions-hollowcandlestick-upColor

The fill color of the candlestick when the current
close is higher than the previous one.

name: plotOptions-hollowcandlestick-upLineColor
title: upLineColor
description:
The color of the line/border of the hollow candlestick when
the current close is higher than the previous one.

name: plotOptions-linearregression-params-xAxisUnit
title: xAxisUnit
description:
Unit (in milliseconds) for the x axis distances used to
compute the regression line parameters (slope & intercept)
for every range. In Highcharts Stock the x axis values are
always represented in milliseconds which may cause that
distances between points are "big" integer numbers.

Highcharts Stock's linear regression algorithm (least squares
method) will utilize these "big" integers for finding the
slope and the intercept of the regression line for each
period. In consequence, this value may be a very "small"
decimal number that's hard to interpret by a human.

For instance: `xAxisUnit` equaled to `86400000` ms (1 day)
forces the algorithm to treat `86400000` as `1` while
computing the slope and the intercept. This may enhance the
legibility of the indicator's values.

Default value is the closest distance between two data
points.

In `v9.0.2`, the default value has been changed
from `undefined` to `null`.

name: plotOptions-scatter-jitter
title: jitter
description:
Apply a jitter effect for the rendered markers. When plotting
discrete values, a little random noise may help telling the points
apart. The jitter setting applies a random displacement of up to `n`
axis units in either direction. So for example on a horizontal X
axis, setting the `jitter.x` to 0.24 will render the point in a
random position between 0.24 units to the left and 0.24 units to the
right of the true axis position. On a category axis, setting it to
0.5 will fill up the bin and make the data appear continuous.

When rendered on top of a box plot or a column series, a jitter value
of 0.24 will correspond to the underlying series' default
[groupPadding](https://api.highcharts.com/highcharts/plotOptions.column.groupPadding)
and [pointPadding](https://api.highcharts.com/highcharts/plotOptions.column.pointPadding)
settings.

**Note:** With boost mode enabled, the jitter effect is not supported.

name: plotOptions-scatter-jitter-x

name: plotOptions-scatter-jitter-y
title: y
description: The maximal Y offset for the random jitter effect.

name: plotOptions-scatter-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The width of the line connecting the data points.

name: plotOptions-scatter-stickyTracking
title: stickyTracking
description:
Sticky tracking of mouse events. When true, the `mouseOut` event
on a series isn't triggered until the mouse moves over another
series, or out of the plot area. When false, the `mouseOut` event on
a series is triggered when the mouse leaves the area around the
series' graph or markers. This also implies the tooltip. When
`stickyTracking` is false and `tooltip.shared` is false, the tooltip
will be hidden when moving the mouse between series.

name: plotOptions-scatter-tooltip

Overridable properties are `headerFormat`, `pointFormat`,
`yDecimals`, `xDateFormat`, `yPrefix` and `ySuffix`. Unlike other
series, in a scatter plot the series.name by default shows in the
headerFormat and point.x and point.y in the pointFormat.
