title: midiName
description:
Name to use for a track when exporting to MIDI.
By default it uses the series name if the track is related to
a series.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping
title: pointGrouping
description: Options for point grouping, specifically for instrument tracks.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping-algorithm
title: algorithm
description:
The grouping algorithm, deciding which points to keep when
grouping a set of points together. By default `"minmax"` is
used, which keeps both the minimum and maximum points.

The other algorithms will either keep the first point in the
group (time wise), last point, middle point, or both the first
and the last point.

The timing of the resulting point(s) is then adjusted to play
evenly, regardless of its original position within the group.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether or not to group points

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping-groupTimespan
title: groupTimespan
description:
The size of each group in milliseconds. Audio events closer than
this are grouped together.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-pointGrouping-prop
title: prop
description:
The data property for each point to compare when deciding which
points to keep in the group.

By default it is "y", which means that if the `"minmax"`
algorithm is used, the two points the group with the lowest and
highest `y` value will be kept, and the others not played.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-roundToMusicalNotes
title: roundToMusicalNotes
description:
Round pitch mapping to musical notes.

If `false`, will play the exact mapped note, even if it is out
of tune compared to the musical notes as defined by 440Hz
standard tuning.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-showPlayMarker
title: showPlayMarker
description: Show play marker (tooltip and/or crosshair) for a track.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-type
title: type
description:
Type of track. Always `"instrument"` for instrument tracks, and
`"speech"` for speech tracks.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-timeInterval
title: timeInterval
description:
Set a context track to play periodically every `timeInterval`
milliseconds while the sonification is playing.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-valueInterval
title: valueInterval
description:
Set a context track to play periodically every `valueInterval`
units of a data property `valueProp` while the sonification is
playing.

For example, setting `valueProp` to `x` and `valueInterval` to 5
will play the context track for every 5th X value.

The context audio events will be mapped to time according to the
prop value relative to the min/max values for that prop.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-valueMapFunction
title: valueMapFunction
description:
How to map context events to time when using the `valueInterval`
option.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-contextTracks-valueProp
title: valueProp
description: The point property to play context for when using `valueInterval`.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions
title: defaultInstrumentOptions
description: Default options for all this series' instrument tracks.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen
title: activeWhen
description:
Define a condition for when a track should be active and not.

Can either be a function callback or a configuration object.

If a function is used, it should return a `boolean` for whether
or not the track should be active. The function is called for
each audio event, and receives a parameter object with `time`,
and potentially `point` and `value` properties depending on the
track. `point` is available if the audio event is related to a
data point. `value` is available if the track is used as a
context track, and `valueInterval` is used.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-crossingDown
title: crossingDown
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was above, and is now at or
below this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-crossingUp
title: crossingUp
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was below, and is now at or
above this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-max
title: max
description: Track is only active when `prop` is below or at this value.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-min
title: min
description: Track is only active when `prop` is above or at this value.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultInstrumentOptions-activeWhen-prop
title: prop
description: The point property to compare, for example `y` or `x`.

title: lowpass

frequencies, making the sound more dull.

title: frequency

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-mapping-lowpass-resonance
title: resonance
description:

title: noteDuration
description:

milliseconds.

It only affects instruments that are able to play
continuous sustained notes. Examples of these instruments
from the presets include `flute`, `saxophone`, `trumpet`,
`sawsynth`, `wobble`, `basic1`, `basic2`, `sine`,
`sineGlide`, `triangle`, `square`, `sawtooth`, `noise`,

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-mapping-pan
title: pan
description:
Pan refers to the stereo panning position of the sound.
It is defined from -1 (left) to 1 (right).

By default it is mapped to `x`, making the sound move from
left to right as the chart plays.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-mapping-tremolo
title: tremolo
description:
Mapping options for tremolo effects.

Tremolo is repeated changes of volume over time.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-mapping-tremolo-depth
title: depth
description:
Map to tremolo depth, from 0 to 1.

This determines the intensity of the tremolo effect, how
much the volume changes.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-mapping-tremolo-speed
title: speed
description:
Map to tremolo speed, from 0 to 1.

This determines the speed of the tremolo effect, how fast
the volume changes.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-mapping-rate
title: rate
description: Speech rate (speed) multiplier.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-mapping-text
title: text
description:
The text to announce for speech tracks. Can either be a
format string or a function.

If it is a function, it should return the format string to
announce. The function is called for each audio event, and
receives a parameter object with `time`, and potentially
`point` and `value` properties depending on the track.
`point` is available if the audio event is related to a data
point. `value` is available if the track is used as a
context track, and `valueInterval` is used.

If it is a format string, in addition to normal string
content, format values can be accessed using bracket
notation. For example `"Value is {point.y}%"`.

`time`, `point` and `value` are available to the format
strings similarly to with functions. Nested properties can
be accessed with dot notation, for example
`"Density: {point.options.custom.density}"`

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-pointGrouping-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether or not to group points

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-pointGrouping-groupTimespan
title: groupTimespan
description:
The size of each group in milliseconds. Audio events closer than
this are grouped together.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-pointGrouping-prop
title: prop
description:
The data property for each point to compare when deciding which
points to keep in the group.

By default it is "y", which means that if the `"minmax"`
algorithm is used, the two points the group with the lowest and
highest `y` value will be kept, and the others not played.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-showPlayMarker
title: showPlayMarker
description: Show play marker (tooltip and/or crosshair) for a track.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-type
title: type
description:
Type of track. Always `"instrument"` for instrument tracks, and
`"speech"` for speech tracks.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-language
title: language
description:
The language to speak in for speech tracks, as an IETF BCP 47
language tag.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-defaultSpeechOptions-preferredVoice
title: preferredVoice
description:
Name of the voice synthesis to prefer for speech tracks.

If not available, falls back to the default voice for the
selected language.

Different platforms provide different voices for web speech
synthesis.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether or not sonification is enabled for this series.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-pointGrouping
title: pointGrouping
description: Sonification point grouping options for this series.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-pointGrouping-algorithm
title: algorithm
description:
The grouping algorithm, deciding which points to keep when
grouping a set of points together. By default `"minmax"` is
used, which keeps both the minimum and maximum points.

The other algorithms will either keep the first point in the
group (time wise), last point, middle point, or both the first
and the last point.

The timing of the resulting point(s) is then adjusted to play
evenly, regardless of its original position within the group.

title: enabled
description: Whether or not to group points

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-pointGrouping-groupTimespan

algorithm is used, the two points the group with the lowest and

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks
title: tracks
description:
Tracks for this series.

Given as an array of instrument tracks, speech tracks, or a mix of both.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-activeWhen
title: activeWhen
description:
Define a condition for when a track should be active and not.

Can either be a function callback or a configuration object.

If a function is used, it should return a `boolean` for whether
or not the track should be active. The function is called for
each audio event, and receives a parameter object with `time`,
and potentially `point` and `value` properties depending on the
track. `point` is available if the audio event is related to a
data point. `value` is available if the track is used as a
context track, and `valueInterval` is used.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-activeWhen-crossingDown
title: crossingDown
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was above, and is now at or
below this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-activeWhen-crossingUp
title: crossingUp
description:
Track is only active when `prop` was below, and is now at or
above this value.

If both `crossingUp` and `crossingDown` are defined, the track
is active if either condition is met.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-activeWhen-max
title: max
description: Track is only active when `prop` is below or at this value.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-activeWhen-min
title: min
description: Track is only active when `prop` is above or at this value.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-activeWhen-prop

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-mapping-pitch
title: pitch
description:
Musical pitch refers to how high or low notes are played.

By default it is mapped to `y` so low `y` values are played
with a lower pitch, and high values are played with a higher
pitch.

Pitch mapping has a few extra features compared to other
audio parameters.

Firstly, it accepts not only number values, but also string
values denoting note names. These are given in the form
`<note><octave>`, for example `"c6"` or `"F#2"`.

Secondly, it is possible to map pitch to an array of notes.
In this case, the `[gapBetweenNotes](#sonification.defaultInstrumentOptions.mapping.gapBetweenNotes)`
mapping determines the delay between these notes.

Thirdly, it is possible to define a musical scale to follow
when mapping.

Can be set to a fixed value, an array, a prop to map to, a
function, or a mapping object.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-mapping-pitch-scale
title: scale
description:
Map pitches to a musical scale. The scale is defined as an
array of semitone offsets from the root note.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-mapping-playDelay
title: playDelay
description:
Milliseconds to wait before playing, comes in addition to
the time determined by the `time` mapping.

Can also be negative to play before the mapped time.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-mapping-time
title: time
description:
Time mapping determines what time each point plays. It is
defined as an offset in milliseconds, where 0 means it
plays immediately when the chart is sonified.

By default time is mapped to `x`, meaning points with the
lowest `x` value plays first, and points with the highest
`x` value plays last.

Can be set to a fixed value, a prop to map to, a function,
or a mapping object.

title: midiName
description:

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-pointGrouping
title: pointGrouping
description: Options for point grouping, specifically for instrument tracks.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-pointGrouping-algorithm
title: algorithm
description:
The grouping algorithm, deciding which points to keep when
grouping a set of points together. By default `"minmax"` is
used, which keeps both the minimum and maximum points.

The other algorithms will either keep the first point in the
group (time wise), last point, middle point, or both the first

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-roundToMusicalNotes
title: roundToMusicalNotes
description:
Round pitch mapping to musical notes.

If `false`, will play the exact mapped note, even if it is out
of tune compared to the musical notes as defined by 440Hz
standard tuning.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-showPlayMarker
title: showPlayMarker
description: Show play marker (tooltip and/or crosshair) for a track.

name: plotOptions-series-sonification-tracks-type
title: type
description:
Type of track. Always `"instrument"` for instrument tracks, and
`"speech"` for speech tracks.

name: plotOptions-series-stacking
title: stacking
description:
Whether to stack the values of each series on top of each other.
Possible values are null to disable, `"normal"` to stack by
value or `"percent"`.

When stacking is enabled, data must be sorted
in ascending X order.

Some stacking options are related to specific series types. In the
streamgraph series type, the stacking option is set to `"stream"`.
The second one is `"overlap"`, which only applies to waterfall
series.

name: plotOptions-series-states
title: states
description:
A collection of options for different series states.

In addition to the options documented under each state, any option from
the parent series type can be set, with exception of `data` and `states`.

name: plotOptions-series-states-hover
title: hover
description:
Options for the hovered series. These settings override the
normal state options when a series is moused over or touched.

name: plotOptions-series-states-hover-animation
title: animation
description: Animation setting for hovering the graph in line-type series.

name: plotOptions-series-states-hover-animation-duration
title: duration
description:
The duration of the hover animation in milliseconds. By
default the hover state animates quickly in, and slowly
back to normal.

name: plotOptions-series-states-hover-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Enable separate styles for the hovered series to visualize
that the user hovers either the series itself or the legend.

name: plotOptions-series-states-hover-halo
title: halo
description:
Options for the halo appearing around the hovered point in
line-type series as well as outside the hovered slice in pie
charts. By default the halo is filled by the current point or
series color with an opacity of 0.25\. The halo can be
disabled by setting the `halo` option to `null`.

In styled mode, the halo is styled with the
`.highcharts-halo` class, with colors inherited from
`.highcharts-color-{n}`.

name: plotOptions-series-states-hover-halo-attributes
title: attributes
description:
A collection of SVG attributes to override the appearance
of the halo, for example `fill`, `stroke` and
`stroke-width`.

name: plotOptions-series-states-hover-halo-opacity
title: opacity
description:
Opacity for the halo unless a specific fill is overridden
using the `attributes` setting.

name: plotOptions-series-states-hover-halo-size
title: size
description:
The pixel size of the halo. For point markers this is the
radius of the halo. For pie slices it is the width of the
halo outside the slice. For bubbles it defaults to 5 and
is the width of the halo outside the bubble.

name: plotOptions-series-states-hover-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description:
Pixel width of the graph line. By default this property is
undefined, and the `lineWidthPlus` property dictates how much
to increase the linewidth from normal state.

name: plotOptions-series-states-hover-lineWidthPlus
title: lineWidthPlus
description: The additional line width for the graph of a hovered series.

name: plotOptions-series-states-hover-marker
title: marker
description:
In Highcharts 1.0, the appearance of all markers belonging
to the hovered series. For settings on the hover state of the
individual point, see
[marker.states.hover](#plotOptions.series.marker.states.hover).

name: plotOptions-series-states-inactive
title: inactive
description: The opposite state of a hover for series.

name: plotOptions-series-states-inactive-animation
title: animation
description: Animation when not hovering over the marker.

name: plotOptions-series-states-inactive-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the inactive state for a series

name: plotOptions-series-states-inactive-opacity
title: opacity
description: Opacity of series elements (dataLabels, line, area).

name: plotOptions-series-states-normal
title: normal
description:
The normal state of a series, or for point items in column, pie
and similar series. Currently only used for setting animation
when returning to normal state from hover.

name: plotOptions-series-states-normal-animation
title: animation
description: Animation when returning to normal state after hovering.

name: plotOptions-series-states-select
title: select
description:
Specific options for point in selected states, after being
selected by
[allowPointSelect](#plotOptions.series.allowPointSelect)
or programmatically.

name: plotOptions-series-step
title: step
description:
Whether to apply steps to the line. Possible values are `left`,
`center` and `right`.

name: plotOptions-series-stickyTracking
title: stickyTracking
description:
Sticky tracking of mouse events. When true, the `mouseOut` event on a
series isn't triggered until the mouse moves over another series, or
out of the plot area. When false, the `mouseOut` event on a series is
triggered when the mouse leaves the area around the series' graph or
markers. This also implies the tooltip when not shared. When
`stickyTracking` is false and `tooltip.shared` is false, the tooltip
will be hidden when moving the mouse between series. Defaults to true
for line and area type series, but to false for columns, pies etc.

**Note:** The boost module will force this option because of
technical limitations.

name: plotOptions-series-threshold
title: threshold
description:
The threshold, also called zero level or base level. For line type
series this is only used in conjunction with
[negativeColor](#plotOptions.series.negativeColor).

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip
title: tooltip
description:
A configuration object for the tooltip rendering of each single
series. Properties are inherited from [tooltip](#tooltip), but only
the following properties can be defined on a series level.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-changeDecimals
title: changeDecimals
description:
How many decimals to show for the `point.change`
or the `point.cumulativeSum` value when the `series.compare`
or the `series.cumulative` option is set.
This is overridable in each series' tooltip options object.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-clusterFormat
title: clusterFormat
description:
The HTML of the cluster point's in the tooltip. Works only with
marker-clusters module and analogously to
[pointFormat](#tooltip.pointFormat).

The cluster tooltip can be also formatted using
`tooltip.formatter` callback function and `point.isCluster` flag.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-dateTimeLabelFormats
title: dateTimeLabelFormats
description:
For series on datetime axes, the date format in the tooltip's
header will by default be guessed based on the closest data points.
This member gives the default string representations used for
each unit. For an overview of the string or object configuration, see
[dateFormat](/class-reference/Highcharts.Time#dateFormat).

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-distance
title: distance
description: Distance from point to tooltip in pixels.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-followPointer
title: followPointer
description:
Whether the tooltip should follow the mouse as it moves across
columns, pie slices and other point types with an extent.
By default it behaves this way for pie, polygon, map, sankey
and wordcloud series by override in the `plotOptions`
for those series types.

Does not apply if [split](#tooltip.split) is `true`.

For touch moves to behave the same way, [followTouchMove](#tooltip.followTouchMove) must be `true` also.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-followTouchMove
title: followTouchMove
description:
Whether the tooltip should update as the finger moves on a touch
device. If this is `true` and [chart.panning](#chart.panning) is
set,`followTouchMove` will take over one-finger touches, so the user
needs to use two fingers for zooming and panning.

Note the difference to [followPointer](#tooltip.followPointer) that
only defines the _position_ of the tooltip. If `followPointer` is
false in for example a column series, the tooltip will show above or
below the column, but as `followTouchMove` is true, the tooltip will
jump from column to column as the user swipes across the plot area.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-footerFormat
title: footerFormat
description: A string to append to the tooltip format.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-format
title: format
description:
A [format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
for the whole shared tooltip. When format strings are a requirement,
it is usually more convenient to use `headerFormat`, `pointFormat`
and `footerFormat`, but the `format` option allows combining them
into one setting.

The context of the format string is the same as that of the
`tooltip.formatter` callback.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-header
title: header
description:
Options for the tooltip header when [tooltip.split](#tooltip.split)
is enabled. The header is the box containing the X value in a split
tooltip.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-header-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description:
Background color for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-header-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
Border color for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-header-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description:
The width of the border for the tooltip header when
[tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is enabled.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-header-distance
title: distance
description:
Distance between the plot area and the header (except the
chevron) in a split tooltip, in pixels. The default value makes
the header text align with the axis labels.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-header-shape
title: shape
description:
The name of a symbol to use for the border around the tooltip
header. Applies only when [tooltip.split](#tooltip.split) is
enabled.

Custom callbacks for symbol path generation can also be added to
`Highcharts.SVGRenderer.prototype.symbols` the same way as for
[series.marker.symbol](plotOptions.line.marker.symbol).

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-header-style
title: style
description:
CSS styles for the tooltip header. The default is `{ fontSize:
'1em' }`, ensuring that the header text is the same size as the
axis labels.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-headerFormat
title: headerFormat
description:
The HTML of the tooltip header line. The context is the
[Point class](https://api.highcharts.com/class-reference/Highcharts.Point).
Variables are enclosed in curly brackets. Examples of common
variables to include are `x`, `y`, `series.name` and `series.color`
and other properties on the same form. The `point.key` variable
contains the category name, x value or datetime string depending on
the type of axis. For datetime axes, the `point.key` date format can
be set using `tooltip.xDateFormat`.
In v12+, locale-aware date names follow the browser's casing and can
be lower-case, so use the `ucfirst` helper (for example
`{ucfirst point.key}`) if you want a capitalized header.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-nullFormat
title: nullFormat
description:
The HTML of the null point's line in the tooltip. Works analogously
to [pointFormat](#tooltip.pointFormat).

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-nullFormatter
title: nullFormatter
description:
Callback function to format the text of the tooltip for
visible null points.
Works analogously to [formatter](#tooltip.formatter), including the
`ctx` callback argument added in v12.5.0.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-pointFormat
title: pointFormat
description:
The HTML of the point's line in the tooltip. The context is the
[Point class](https://api.highcharts.com/class-reference/Highcharts.Point).
Variables are enclosed in curly brackets. Examples of common
variables to include are `x`, `y`, `series.name` and `series.color`
and other properties on the same form. Furthermore, `y` can be
extended by the `tooltip.valuePrefix` and `tooltip.valueSuffix`
variables. This can also be overridden for each series, which makes
it a good hook for displaying units.

In styled mode, the dot is colored by a class name rather than the
point color.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-pointFormatter
title: pointFormatter
description:
A callback function for formatting the HTML output for a single point
in the tooltip. Like the `pointFormat` string, but with more
flexibility. Since v12.6.0, the callback also receives `ctx` as the
first argument, so that arrow functions can access the same context
as regular functions using `this`.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-position
title: position
description:
Positioning options for fixed tooltip, taking effect only when
[tooltip.fixed](#tooltip.fixed) is `true`.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-position-align
title: align
description: The horizontal alignment of the fixed tooltip.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-position-relativeTo
title: relativeTo
description:
What the fixed tooltip alignment should be relative to.

The default, `pane`, means that it is aligned within the plot
area for that given series. If the tooltip is split (as default
in Stock charts), each partial tooltip is aligned within the
series' pane.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-position-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description: The vertical alignment of the fixed tooltip.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-position-x
title: x
description:
X pixel offset from the given position. Can be used to shy away
from axis lines, grid lines etc to avoid the tooltip overlapping
other elements.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-position-y
title: y
description:
Y pixel offset from the given position. Can be used to shy away
from axis lines, grid lines etc to avoid the tooltip overlapping
other elements.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-showDelay
title: showDelay
description:
The number of milliseconds to wait until the tooltip is shown when
mouse over a point. Works on initial hover.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-valueDecimals
title: valueDecimals
description:
How many decimals to show in each series' y value. This is
overridable in each series' tooltip options object. The default is to
preserve all decimals.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-valuePrefix
title: valuePrefix
description:
A string to prepend to each series' y value. Overridable in each
series' tooltip options object.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-valueSuffix
title: valueSuffix
description:
A string to append to each series' y value. Overridable in each
series' tooltip options object.

name: plotOptions-series-tooltip-xDateFormat
title: xDateFormat
description:
The format for the date in the tooltip header if the X axis is a
datetime axis. The default is a best guess based on the smallest
distance between points in the chart.

name: plotOptions-series-turboThreshold
title: turboThreshold
description:
When a series contains a `data` array that is longer than this, the
Series class looks for data configurations of plain numbers or arrays of
numbers. The first and last valid points are checked. If found, the rest
of the data is assumed to be the same. This saves expensive data checking
and indexing in long series, and makes data-heavy charts render faster.

Set it to `0` disable.

Note:
- In boost mode turbo threshold is forced. Only array of numbers or two
  dimensional arrays are allowed.
- In version 11.4.3 and earlier, if object configurations were passed
  beyond the turbo threshold, a warning was logged in the console and the
  data series didn't render.

name: plotOptions-series-useOhlcData
title: useOhlcData
description:
The parameter allows setting line series type and use OHLC indicators.
Data in OHLC format is required.

name: plotOptions-series-visible
title: visible
description: Set the initial visibility of the series.

name: plotOptions-series-zoneAxis
title: zoneAxis
description: Defines the Axis on which the zones are applied.

name: plotOptions-series-zones
title: zones
description:
An array defining zones within a series. Zones can be applied to the
X axis, Y axis or Z axis for bubbles, according to the `zoneAxis`
option. The zone definitions have to be in ascending order regarding
to the value.

In styled mode, the color zones are styled with the
`.highcharts-zone-{n}` class, or custom classed from the `className`
option
([view live demo](https://jsfiddle.net/gh/get/library/pure/highcharts/highcharts/tree/master/samples/highcharts/css/color-zones/)).

name: plotOptions-series-zones-className
title: className
description: Styled mode only. A custom class name for the zone.

name: plotOptions-series-zones-color
title: color
description: Defines the color of the series.

name: plotOptions-series-zones-dashStyle
title: dashStyle
description: A name for the dash style to use for the graph.

name: plotOptions-series-zones-fillColor
title: fillColor
description: Defines the fill color for the series (in area type series)

name: plotOptions-series-zones-value
title: value
description:
The value up to where the zone extends, if undefined the zones
stretches to the last value in the series.

name: plotOptions-series-zoomEnabled
title: zoomEnabled
description:
Whether to zoom non-cartesian series. If `chart.zooming` is set, the option
allows to disable zooming on an individual non-cartesian series. By default
zooming is enabled for all series.

**Note**: This option works only for non-cartesian series.

name: plotOptions-slowstochastic
title: slowstochastic

name: plotOptions-slowstochastic-params-periods
title: periods
description: Periods for Slow Stochastic oscillator: [%K, %D, SMA(%D)].

name: plotOptions-sma
title: sma

name: plotOptions-sma-compareToMain
title: compareToMain
description:
Whether to compare indicator to the main series values
or indicator values.

name: plotOptions-sma-linkedTo
title: linkedTo
description:
The main series ID that indicator will be based on. Required for this
indicator.

name: plotOptions-sma-name
title: name
description:
The name of the series as shown in the legend, tooltip etc. If not
set, it will be based on a technical indicator type and default
params.

name: plotOptions-sma-params
title: params
description: Parameters used in calculation of regression series' points.

name: plotOptions-sma-params-index
title: index
description:
The point index which indicator calculations will base. For
example using OHLC data, index=2 means the indicator will be
calculated using Low values.

name: plotOptions-sma-params-period
title: period
description:
The base period for indicator calculations. This is the number of
data points which are taken into account for the indicator
calculations.

name: plotOptions-sma-tooltip-valueDecimals
title: valueDecimals
description: Number of decimals in indicator series.

name: plotOptions-spline
title: spline

name: plotOptions-stochastic
title: stochastic

name: plotOptions-stochastic-params-periods
title: periods
description: Periods for Stochastic oscillator: [%K, %D].

name: plotOptions-stochastic-smoothedLine
title: smoothedLine
description: Smoothed line options.

name: plotOptions-stochastic-smoothedLine-styles
title: styles
description: Styles for a smoothed line.

name: plotOptions-stochastic-smoothedLine-styles-lineColor
title: lineColor
description:
Color of the line. If not set, it's inherited from
[plotOptions.stochastic.color](#plotOptions.stochastic.color).

name: plotOptions-stochastic-smoothedLine-styles-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: Pixel width of the line.

name: plotOptions-streamgraph
title: streamgraph

name: plotOptions-supertrend
title: supertrend

name: plotOptions-supertrend-changeTrendLine
title: changeTrendLine
description: The styles for the Supertrend line that intersect main series.

name: plotOptions-supertrend-changeTrendLine-styles-dashStyle
title: dashStyle
description:
The dash or dot style of the grid lines. For possible
values, see
[this demonstration](https://jsfiddle.net/gh/get/library/pure/highcharts/highcharts/tree/master/samples/highcharts/plotoptions/series-dashstyle-all/).

name: plotOptions-supertrend-changeTrendLine-styles-lineColor
title: lineColor
description: Color of the line.

name: plotOptions-supertrend-changeTrendLine-styles-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: Pixel width of the line.

name: plotOptions-supertrend-fallingTrendColor
title: fallingTrendColor
description: Color of the Supertrend series line that is above the main series.

name: plotOptions-supertrend-params
title: params
description: Parameters used in calculation of Supertrend indicator series points.

name: plotOptions-supertrend-params-multiplier
title: multiplier
description: Multiplier for Supertrend Indicator.

name: plotOptions-supertrend-params-period
title: period
description:
The base period for indicator Supertrend Indicator calculations.
This is the number of data points which are taken into account
for the indicator calculations.

name: plotOptions-supertrend-risingTrendColor
title: risingTrendColor
description: Color of the Supertrend series line that is beneath the main series.

name: plotOptions-tema
title: tema

name: plotOptions-trendline
title: trendline

name: plotOptions-trendline-params-index
title: index
description:
The point index which indicator calculations will base. For
example using OHLC data, index=2 means the indicator will be
calculated using Low values.

name: plotOptions-trix
title: trix

name: plotOptions-vbp
title: vbp

name: plotOptions-vbp-params-ranges
title: ranges
description: The number of price zones.

name: plotOptions-vbp-params-volumeSeriesID
title: volumeSeriesID
description:
The id of volume series which is mandatory. For example using
OHLC data, volumeSeriesID='volume' means the indicator will be
calculated using OHLC and volume values.

name: plotOptions-vbp-volumeDivision
title: volumeDivision
description: The styles for bars when volume is divided into positive/negative.

name: plotOptions-vbp-volumeDivision-enabled
title: enabled
description: Option to control if volume is divided.

name: plotOptions-vbp-volumeDivision-styles-negativeColor
title: negativeColor
description: Color of negative volume bars.

name: plotOptions-vbp-volumeDivision-styles-positiveColor
title: positiveColor
description: Color of positive volume bars.

name: plotOptions-vbp-zoneLines
title: zoneLines
description: The styles for lines which determine price zones.

name: plotOptions-vbp-zoneLines-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable/disable zone lines.

name: plotOptions-vbp-zoneLines-styles
title: styles
description: Specify the style of zone lines.

name: plotOptions-vector
title: vector

name: plotOptions-vector-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The line width for each vector arrow.

name: plotOptions-vector-rotationOrigin
title: rotationOrigin
description:
What part of the vector it should be rotated around. Can be one of
`start`, `center` and `end`. When `start`, the vectors will start
from the given [x, y] position, and when `end` the vectors will end
in the [x, y] position.

name: plotOptions-vector-states-hover-lineWidthPlus
title: lineWidthPlus
description:
Additional line width for the vector errors when they are
hovered.

name: plotOptions-vector-vectorLength
title: vectorLength
description:
Maximum length of the arrows in the vector plot. The individual arrow
length is computed between 0 and this value.

name: plotOptions-vwap
title: vwap

name: plotOptions-vwap-params-volumeSeriesID
title: volumeSeriesID
description:
The id of volume series which is mandatory. For example using
OHLC data, volumeSeriesID='volume' means the indicator will be
calculated using OHLC and volume values.

name: plotOptions-williamsr
title: williamsr

name: plotOptions-williamsr-params
title: params
description: Parameters used in calculation of Williams %R series points.

name: plotOptions-williamsr-params-period
title: period
description: Period for Williams %R oscillator

name: plotOptions-windbarb
title: windbarb

name: plotOptions-windbarb-dataGrouping
title: dataGrouping
description:
Data grouping options for the wind barbs. In Highcharts, this
requires the `modules/datagrouping.js` module to be loaded. In
Highcharts Stock, data grouping is included.

name: plotOptions-windbarb-dataGrouping-approximation
title: approximation
description:
Approximation function for the data grouping. The default
returns an average of wind speed and a vector average direction
weighted by wind speed.

name: plotOptions-windbarb-dataGrouping-enabled
title: enabled
description: Whether to enable data grouping.

name: plotOptions-windbarb-dataGrouping-groupPixelWidth
title: groupPixelWidth
description: The approximate data group width.

name: plotOptions-windbarb-lineWidth
title: lineWidth
description: The line width of the wind barb symbols.

name: plotOptions-windbarb-onSeries
title: onSeries
description:
The id of another series in the chart that the wind barbs are
projected on. When `null`, the wind symbols are drawn on the X axis,
but offset up or down by the `yOffset` setting.

name: plotOptions-windbarb-tooltip-pointFormat
title: pointFormat
description:
The default point format for the wind barb tooltip. Note the
`point.beaufort` property that refers to the Beaufort wind scale.
The names can be internationalized by modifying
`Highcharts.seriesTypes.windbarb.prototype.beaufortNames`.

name: plotOptions-windbarb-vectorLength
title: vectorLength
description: Pixel length of the stems.

name: plotOptions-windbarb-xOffset
title: xOffset
description:
Horizontal offset from the cartesian position, in pixels. When the
chart is inverted, this option allows translation like
[yOffset](#plotOptions.windbarb.yOffset) in non inverted charts.

name: plotOptions-windbarb-yOffset
title: yOffset
description:
Vertical offset from the cartesian position, in pixels. The default
value makes sure the symbols don't overlap the X axis when `onSeries`
is `null`, and that they don't overlap the linked series when
`onSeries` is given.

name: plotOptions-wma
title: wma

name: plotOptions-xrange
title: xrange

name: plotOptions-xrange-colorByPoint
title: colorByPoint
description:
In an X-range series, this option makes all points of the same Y-axis
category the same color.

name: plotOptions-xrange-dragDrop-draggableX1
title: draggableX1
description: Allow x value to be dragged individually.

name: plotOptions-xrange-dragDrop-draggableX2
title: draggableX2
description: Allow x2 value to be dragged individually.

name: plotOptions-xrange-partialFill
title: partialFill
description:
A partial fill for each point, typically used to visualize how much
of a task is performed. The partial fill object can be set either on
series or point level. When set as a number, works as
`{ amount: number }`.

name: plotOptions-xrange-partialFill-fill
title: fill
description:
The fill color to be used for partial fills. Defaults to a darker
shade of the point color.

name: plotOptions-zigzag
title: zigzag

name: plotOptions-zigzag-params-deviation
title: deviation
description:
The threshold for the value change.

For example deviation=1 means the indicator will ignore all price
movements less than 1%.

name: plotOptions-zigzag-params-highIndex
title: highIndex
description:
The point index which indicator calculations will base - high
value.

For example using OHLC data, index=1 means the indicator will be
calculated using High values.

name: plotOptions-zigzag-params-lowIndex
title: lowIndex
description:
The point index which indicator calculations will base - low
value.

For example using OHLC data, index=2 means the indicator will be
calculated using Low values.

name: rangeSelector
title: rangeSelector
description:
The range selector is a tool for selecting ranges to display within
the chart. It provides buttons to select preconfigured ranges in
the chart, like 1 day, 1 week, 1 month etc. It also provides input
boxes where min and max dates can be manually input.

name: rangeSelector-allButtonsEnabled
title: allButtonsEnabled
description:
Whether to enable all buttons from the start. By default buttons are
only enabled if the corresponding time range exists on the X axis,
but enabling all buttons allows for dynamically loading different
time ranges.

name: rangeSelector-buttonPosition
title: buttonPosition
description: Positioning for the button row.

name: rangeSelector-buttonPosition-align
title: align
description:
The alignment of the input box. Allowed properties are `left`,
`center`, `right`.

name: rangeSelector-buttonPosition-x
title: x
description: X offset of the button row.

name: rangeSelector-buttonPosition-y
title: y
description: Y offset of the button row.

name: rangeSelector-buttonSpacing
title: buttonSpacing
description: The space in pixels between the buttons in the range selector.

name: rangeSelector-buttonTheme
title: buttonTheme
description:
A collection of attributes for the buttons. The object takes SVG
attributes like `fill`, `stroke`, `stroke-width`, as well as `style`,
a collection of CSS properties for the text.

The object can also be extended with states, so you can set
presentational options for `hover`, `select` or `disabled` button
states.

CSS styles for the text label.

In styled mode, the buttons are styled by the
`.highcharts-range-selector-buttons .highcharts-button` rule with its
different states.

name: rangeSelector-buttons
title: buttons

name: rangeSelector-buttons-count
title: count
description:
How many units of the defined type the button should span. If `type`
is "month" and `count` is 3, the button spans three months.

name: rangeSelector-buttons-dataGrouping
title: dataGrouping
description: A custom data grouping object for each button.

name: rangeSelector-buttons-events-click
title: click

name: rangeSelector-buttons-offsetMax
title: offsetMax
description:
Additional range (in milliseconds) added to the end of the calculated
time span.

name: rangeSelector-buttons-offsetMin
title: offsetMin
description:
Additional range (in milliseconds) added to the start of the
calculated time span.

name: rangeSelector-buttons-preserveDataGrouping
title: preserveDataGrouping
description:
When buttons apply dataGrouping on a series, by default zooming
in/out will deselect buttons and unset dataGrouping. Enable this
option to keep buttons selected when extremes change.

name: rangeSelector-buttons-text
title: text
description: The text for the button itself.

name: rangeSelector-buttons-title
title: title
description:
Explanation for the button, shown as a tooltip on hover, and used by
assistive technology.

name: rangeSelector-buttons-type
title: type
description:
Defined the time span for the button. Can be one of `millisecond`,
`second`, `minute`, `hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`, `year`, `ytd`,
and `all`.

name: rangeSelector-dropdown
title: dropdown
description:
Whether to collapse the range selector buttons into a dropdown when
there is not enough room to show everything in a single row, instead
of dividing the range selector into multiple rows.
Can be one of the following:
 - `always`: Always collapse
 - `responsive`: Only collapse when there is not enough room
 - `never`: Never collapse

name: rangeSelector-enabled
title: enabled
description:
Enable or disable the range selector. Default to `true` for stock
charts, using the `stockChart` factory.

name: rangeSelector-floating
title: floating
description:
When the rangeselector is floating, the plot area does not reserve
space for it. This opens for positioning anywhere on the chart.

name: rangeSelector-inputBoxBorderColor
title: inputBoxBorderColor
description: The border color of the date input boxes.

name: rangeSelector-inputBoxHeight
title: inputBoxHeight
description: The pixel height of the date input boxes.

name: rangeSelector-inputBoxWidth
title: inputBoxWidth
description:
The pixel width of the date input boxes. When `undefined`, the width
is fitted to the rendered content.

name: rangeSelector-inputDateFormat
title: inputDateFormat
description:
The date format in the input boxes when not selected for editing.
Defaults to `%e %b %Y`.

This is used to determine which type of input to show,
`datetime-local`, `date` or `time` and falling back to `text` when
the browser does not support the input type or the format contains
milliseconds.

name: rangeSelector-inputDateParser
title: inputDateParser
description:
A custom callback function to parse values entered in the input boxes and
return a valid JavaScript time as milliseconds since 1970. The first
argument passed is the value to parse, second is a boolean indicating use
of UTC time. The third is a reference to the `time` object. Time zone can
be read from `time.timezone`.

This will only get called for inputs of type `text`. Since v8.2.3, the
input type is dynamically determined based on the granularity of the
`inputDateFormat` and the browser support.

name: rangeSelector-inputEditDateFormat
title: inputEditDateFormat
description:
The date format in the input boxes when they are selected for
editing. This must be a format that is recognized by JavaScript
Date.parse.

This will only be used for inputs of type `text`. Since v8.2.3,
the input type is dynamically determined based on the granularity
of the `inputDateFormat` and the browser support.

name: rangeSelector-inputEnabled
title: inputEnabled
description: Enable or disable the date input boxes.

name: rangeSelector-inputPosition
title: inputPosition
description:
Positioning for the input boxes. Allowed properties are `align`,
 `x` and `y`.

name: rangeSelector-inputPosition-align
title: align
description:
The alignment of the input box. Allowed properties are `left`,
`center`, `right`.

name: rangeSelector-inputPosition-x
title: x
description: X offset of the input row.

name: rangeSelector-inputPosition-y
title: y
description: Y offset of the input row.

name: rangeSelector-inputSpacing
title: inputSpacing
description:
The space in pixels between the labels and the date input boxes in
the range selector.

name: rangeSelector-inputStyle
title: inputStyle
description:
CSS for the HTML inputs in the range selector.

In styled mode, the inputs are styled by the
`.highcharts-range-input text` rule in SVG mode, and
`input.highcharts-range-selector` when active.

name: rangeSelector-labelStyle
title: labelStyle
description:
CSS styles for the labels - the Zoom, From and To texts.

In styled mode, the labels are styled by the
`.highcharts-range-label` class.

name: rangeSelector-selected
title: selected
description:
The index of the button to appear pre-selected. If the selected range
exceeds the total data range and the 'all' option is available,
the 'all' option, showing the full range, is automatically selected.

name: rangeSelector-verticalAlign
title: verticalAlign
description:
The vertical alignment of the rangeselector box. Allowed properties
are `top`, `middle`, `bottom`.

name: rangeSelector-x
title: x
description:
The x offset of the range selector relative to its horizontal
alignment within `chart.spacingLeft` and `chart.spacingRight`.

name: rangeSelector-y
title: y
description:
The y offset of the range selector relative to its horizontal
alignment within `chart.spacingLeft` and `chart.spacingRight`.

name: responsive
title: responsive
description:
Allows setting a set of rules to apply for different screen or chart
sizes. Each rule specifies additional chart options.

name: responsive-rules
title: rules
description:
A set of rules for responsive settings. The rules are executed from
the top down.

name: responsive-rules-chartOptions
title: chartOptions
description:
A full set of chart options to apply as overrides to the general
chart options. The chart options are applied when the given rule
is active.

A special case is configuration objects that take arrays, for example
[xAxis](#xAxis), [yAxis](#yAxis) or [series](#series). For these
collections, an `id` option is used to map the new option set to
an existing object. If an existing object of the same id is not found,
the item of the same index updated. So for example, setting `chartOptions`
with two series items without an `id`, will cause the existing chart's
two series to be updated with respective options.

name: responsive-rules-condition
title: condition
description: Under which conditions the rule applies.

name: responsive-rules-condition-callback
title: callback
description:
A callback function to gain complete control on when the responsive
rule applies. Return `true` if it applies. This opens for checking
against other metrics than the chart size, for example the document
size or other elements. Since v12.6.0, the callback also receives `ctx`
as the first argument, so that arrow functions can access the same
context as regular functions using `this`.

name: responsive-rules-condition-maxHeight
title: maxHeight
description: The responsive rule applies if the chart height is less than this.

name: responsive-rules-condition-maxWidth
title: maxWidth
description: The responsive rule applies if the chart width is less than this.

name: responsive-rules-condition-minHeight
title: minHeight
description: The responsive rule applies if the chart height is greater than this.

name: responsive-rules-condition-minWidth
title: minWidth
description: The responsive rule applies if the chart width is greater than this.

name: scrollbar
title: scrollbar
description:
The scrollbar is a means of panning over the X axis of a stock chart.
Scrollbars can also be applied to other types of axes.

Another approach to scrollable charts is the [chart.scrollablePlotArea](https://api.highcharts.com/highcharts/chart.scrollablePlotArea) option that
is especially suitable for simpler cartesian charts on mobile.

In styled mode, all the presentational options for the
scrollbar are replaced by the classes `.highcharts-scrollbar-thumb`,
`.highcharts-scrollbar-arrow`, `.highcharts-scrollbar-button`,
`.highcharts-scrollbar-rifles` and `.highcharts-scrollbar-track`.

name: scrollbar-barBackgroundColor
title: barBackgroundColor
description: The background color of the scrollbar itself.

name: scrollbar-barBorderColor
title: barBorderColor
description: The color of the scrollbar's border.

name: scrollbar-barBorderRadius
title: barBorderRadius
description: The border rounding radius of the bar.

name: scrollbar-barBorderWidth
title: barBorderWidth
description: The width of the bar's border.

name: scrollbar-buttonArrowColor
title: buttonArrowColor
description: The color of the small arrow inside the scrollbar buttons.

name: scrollbar-buttonBackgroundColor
title: buttonBackgroundColor
description: The color of scrollbar buttons.

name: scrollbar-buttonBorderColor
title: buttonBorderColor
description: The color of the border of the scrollbar buttons.

name: scrollbar-buttonBorderRadius
title: buttonBorderRadius
description: The corner radius of the scrollbar buttons.

name: scrollbar-buttonBorderWidth
title: buttonBorderWidth
description: The border width of the scrollbar buttons.

name: scrollbar-buttonsEnabled
title: buttonsEnabled
description: Enable or disable the buttons at the end of the scrollbar.

name: scrollbar-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable the scrollbar.

name: scrollbar-height
title: height
description:
The height of the scrollbar. If `buttonsEnabled` is true, the height
also applies to the width of the scroll arrows so that they are always
squares.

name: scrollbar-liveRedraw
title: liveRedraw
description:
Whether to redraw the main chart as the scrollbar or the navigator
zoomed window is moved. Defaults to `true` for modern browsers and
`false` for legacy IE browsers as well as mobile devices. This option
works regardless of whether the scrollbar is enabled or not.

name: scrollbar-margin
title: margin
description:
The margin between the scrollbar and its axis when the scrollbar is
applied directly to an axis, or the navigator in case that is enabled.
Defaults to 10 for axis, 3 for navigator.

name: scrollbar-minWidth
title: minWidth
description: The minimum width of the scrollbar.

name: scrollbar-rifleColor
title: rifleColor
description: The color of the small rifles in the middle of the scrollbar.

name: scrollbar-showFull
title: showFull
description:
Whether to show or hide the scrollbar when the scrolled content is
zoomed out to it full extent.

name: scrollbar-trackBackgroundColor
title: trackBackgroundColor
description: The color of the track background.

name: scrollbar-trackBorderColor
title: trackBorderColor
description: The color of the border of the scrollbar track.

name: scrollbar-trackBorderRadius
title: trackBorderRadius
description: The corner radius of the border of the scrollbar track.

name: scrollbar-trackBorderWidth
title: trackBorderWidth
description: The width of the border of the scrollbar track.

name: scrollbar-zIndex
title: zIndex
description: The z index of the scrollbar group.

name: series
title: series

name: series-accessibility
title: accessibility
description: Accessibility options for a series.

name: series-accessibility-description
title: description
description: Provide a description of the series, announced to screen readers.

name: series-accessibility-descriptionFormat
title: descriptionFormat
description:
Format to use for describing the data series group to assistive
technology - including screen readers.

name: series-accessibility-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable/disable accessibility functionality for a specific series.

name: series-accessibility-exposeAsGroupOnly
title: exposeAsGroupOnly
description: Expose only the series element to screen readers, not its points.

name: series-accessibility-keyboardNavigation
title: keyboardNavigation
description: Keyboard navigation for a series

name: series-accessibility-keyboardNavigation-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable/disable keyboard navigation support for a specific series.

name: series-accessibility-point
title: point
description: Point accessibility options for a series.

name: series-accessibility-point-dateFormat
title: dateFormat
description:
Date format to use for points on datetime axes when describing
them to screen reader users.

Defaults to the same format as in tooltip.

For an overview of the replacement codes, see
[dateFormat](/class-reference/Highcharts.Time#dateFormat).

name: series-accessibility-point-dateFormatter
title: dateFormatter
description:
Formatter function to determine the date/time format used with
points on datetime axes when describing them to screen reader
users. Receives one argument, `point`, referring to the point
to describe. Should return a date format string compatible with
[dateFormat](/class-reference/Highcharts.Time#dateFormat).

name: series-accessibility-point-describeNull
title: describeNull
description:
Whether or not to describe points with the value `null` to
assistive technology, such as screen readers.

name: series-accessibility-point-descriptionFormat
title: descriptionFormat
description:
A [format string](https://www.highcharts.com/docs/chart-concepts/labels-and-string-formatting)
to use instead of the default for point descriptions.

The context of the format string is the point instance.

As opposed to [accessibility.point.valueDescriptionFormat](#accessibility.point.valueDescriptionFormat),
this option replaces the whole description.

name: series-accessibility-point-descriptionFormatter
title: descriptionFormatter
description:
Formatter function to use instead of the default for point
descriptions. Same as `accessibility.point.descriptionFormatter`, but
applies to a series instead of the whole chart.

Note: Prefer using [accessibility.point.valueDescriptionFormat](#plotOptions.series.accessibility.point.valueDescriptionFormat)
instead if possible, as default functionality such as describing
annotations will be preserved.

name: series-accessibility-point-valueDecimals
title: valueDecimals
description:
Decimals to use for the values in the point descriptions. Uses
[tooltip.valueDecimals](#tooltip.valueDecimals) if not defined.

name: series-accessibility-point-valueDescriptionFormat
title: valueDescriptionFormat
description:
Format to use for describing the values of data points
to assistive technology - including screen readers.
The point context is available as `{point}`.

Other available context variables include `{index}`, `{value}`, and `{xDescription}`.

Additionally, the series name, annotation info, and
description added in `point.accessibility.description`
is added by default if relevant. To override this, use the
[accessibility.point.descriptionFormatter](#accessibility.point.descriptionFormatter)
option.

name: series-accessibility-point-valuePrefix
title: valuePrefix
description:
Prefix to add to the values in the point descriptions. Uses
[tooltip.valuePrefix](#tooltip.valuePrefix) if not defined.

name: series-accessibility-point-valueSuffix
title: valueSuffix
description:
Suffix to add to the values in the point descriptions. Uses
[tooltip.valueSuffix](#tooltip.valueSuffix) if not defined.

name: series-allowPointSelect
title: allowPointSelect
description:
Allow this series' points to be selected by clicking on the graphic
(columns, point markers, pie slices, map areas etc).

The selected points can be handled by point select and unselect
events, or collectively by the [getSelectedPoints](/class-reference/Highcharts.Chart#getSelectedPoints) function.

And alternative way of selecting points is through dragging.

name: series-animation
title: animation
description:
Enable or disable the initial animation when a series is displayed.
The animation can also be set as a configuration object. Please
note that this option only applies to the initial animation of the
series itself. For other animations, see [chart.animation](#chart.animation) and the animation parameter under the API methods.
The following properties are supported:

- `defer`: The animation delay time in milliseconds.

- `duration`: The duration of the animation in milliseconds. (Defaults to
  `1000`)

- `easing`: Can be a string reference to an easing function set on
  the `Math` object or a function. See the _Custom easing function_
  demo below. (Defaults to `easeInOutSine`)

Due to poor performance, animation is disabled in old IE browsers
for several chart types.

name: series-animationLimit
title: animationLimit
description:
For some series, there is a limit that shuts down animation
by default when the total number of points in the chart is too high.
For example, for a column chart and its derivatives, animation does
not run if there is more than 250 points totally. To disable this
cap, set `animationLimit` to `Infinity`. This option works if animation
is fired on individual points, not on a group of points like e.g. during
the initial animation.

name: series-boostBlending
title: boostBlending
description: Sets the color blending in the boost module.

name: series-boostThreshold
title: boostThreshold
description:
Set the point threshold for when a series should enter boost mode.

Setting it to e.g. 2000 will cause the series to enter boost mode when there
are 2000 or more points in the series.

To disable boosting on the series, set the `boostThreshold` to 0. Setting it
to 1 will force boosting.

Note that the [cropThreshold](plotOptions.series.cropThreshold) also affects
this setting. When zooming in on a series that has fewer points than the
`cropThreshold`, all points are rendered although outside the visible plot
area, and the `boostThreshold` won't take effect.

name: series-className
title: className
description:
An additional class name to apply to the series' graphical elements.
This option does not replace default class names of the graphical
element. Changes to the series' color will also be reflected in a
chart's legend and tooltip.

name: series-clip
title: clip
description:
Disable this option to allow series rendering in the whole plotting
area.

**Note:** Clipping should be always enabled when
[chart.zoomType](#chart.zoomType) is set

name: series-color
title: color
description:
The main color of the series. In line type series it applies to the
line and the point markers unless otherwise specified. In bar type
series it applies to the bars unless a color is specified per point.
The default value is pulled from the `options.colors` array.

In styled mode, the color can be defined by the
[colorIndex](#plotOptions.series.colorIndex) option. Also, the series
color can be set with the `.highcharts-series`,
`.highcharts-color-{n}`, `.highcharts-{type}-series` or
`.highcharts-series-{n}` class, or individual classes given by the
`className` option.

name: series-colorAxis
title: colorAxis
description:
When using dual or multiple color axes, this number defines which
colorAxis the particular series is connected to. It refers to
either the
{@link #colorAxis.id|axis id}
or the index of the axis in the colorAxis array, with 0 being the
first. Set this option to false to prevent a series from connecting
to the default color axis.

Since v7.2.0 the option can also be an axis id or an axis index
instead of a boolean flag.

name: series-colorIndex
title: colorIndex
description:
Styled mode only. A specific color index to use for the series, so its
graphic representations are given the class name `highcharts-color-{n}`.

Since v11, CSS variables on the form `--highcharts-color-{n}` make
changing the color scheme very convenient.

name: series-colorKey
title: colorKey
description:
Determines what data value should be used to calculate point color
if `colorAxis` is used. Requires to set `min` and `max` if some
custom point property is used or if approximation for data grouping
is set to `'sum'`.

name: series-compare
title: compare
description:
Compare the values of the series against the first non-null, non-
zero value in the visible range. The y axis will show percentage
or absolute change depending on whether `compare` is set to `"percent"`
or `"value"`. When this is applied to multiple series, it allows
comparing the development of the series against each other. Adds
a `change` field to every point object. If a `compare` value is not set on a
linked series, it will be inherited from the parent series.

name: series-compareBase
title: compareBase
description:
When [compare](#plotOptions.series.compare) is `percent`, this option
dictates whether to use 0 or 100 as the base of comparison.

name: series-compareStart
title: compareStart
description:
Defines if comparison should start from the first point within the visible
range or should start from the last point **before** the range.

In other words, this flag determines if first point within the visible range
will have 0% (`compareStart=true`) or should have been already calculated
according to the previous point (`compareStart=false`).

name: series-connectNulls
title: connectNulls
description:
Whether to connect a graph line across null points, or render a gap
between the two points on either side of the null.

In stacked area chart, if `connectNulls` is set to true,
null points are interpreted as 0.

name: series-crisp
title: crisp
description:
When true, each point or column edge is rounded to its nearest pixel
in order to render sharp on screen. In some cases, when there are a
lot of densely packed columns, this leads to visible difference
in column widths or distance between columns. In these cases,
setting `crisp` to `false` may look better, even though each column
is rendered blurry.

name: series-cropThreshold
title: cropThreshold
description:
When the series contains less points than the crop threshold, all
points are drawn, even if the points fall outside the visible plot
area at the current zoom. The advantage of drawing all points
(including markers and columns), is that animation is performed on
updates. On the other hand, when the series contains more points than
the crop threshold, the series data is cropped to only contain points
that fall within the plot area. The advantage of cropping away
invisible points is to increase performance on large series.

name: series-cumulative
title: cumulative
description:
Cumulative Sum feature replaces points' values with the following formula:
`sum of all previous points' values + current point's value`.
Works only for points in a visible range.
Adds the `cumulativeSum` field to each point object that can be accessed
e.g. in the [tooltip.pointFormat](https://api.highcharts.com/highstock/tooltip.pointFormat).

With `dataGrouping` enabled, default grouping approximation is set to `sum`.

name: series-cumulativeStart
title: cumulativeStart
description:
Defines if cumulation should start from the first point within the visible
range or should start from the last point **before** the range.

In other words, this flag determines if first point within the visible range
will start at 0 (`cumulativeStart=true`) or should have been already calculated
according to the previous point (`cumulativeStart=false`).

name: series-cursor
title: cursor
description:
You can set the cursor to "pointer" if you have click events attached
to the series, to signal to the user that the points and lines can
be clicked.

In styled mode, the series cursor can be set with the same classes
as listed under [series.color](#plotOptions.series.color).

name: series-custom
title: custom
description:
A reserved subspace to store options and values for customized
functionality. Here you can add additional data for your own event
callbacks and formatter callbacks.

name: series-dashStyle
title: dashStyle
description:
Name of the dash style to use for the graph, or for some series types
the outline of each shape.

In styled mode, the
[stroke dash-array](https://jsfiddle.net/gh/get/library/pure/highcharts/highcharts/tree/master/samples/highcharts/css/series-dashstyle/)
can be set with the same classes as listed under
[series.color](#plotOptions.series.color).

name: series-dataGrouping
title: dataGrouping
description:
Data grouping is the concept of sampling the data values into larger
blocks in order to ease readability and increase performance of the
JavaScript charts. Highcharts Stock by default applies data grouping when
the points become closer than a certain pixel value, determined by
the `groupPixelWidth` option.

If data grouping is applied, the grouping information of grouped
points can be read from the [Point.dataGroup](/class-reference/Highcharts.Point#dataGroup). If point options other than
the data itself are set, for example `name` or `color` or custom properties,
the grouping logic doesn't know how to group it. In this case the options of
the first point instance are copied over to the group point. This can be
altered through a custom `approximation` callback function.

name: series-dataGrouping-anchor
title: anchor
description:
Specifies how the points should be located on the X axis inside the group.
Points that are extremes can be set separately. Available options:

- `start` places the point at the beginning of the group
(e.g. range 00:00:00 - 23:59:59 -> 00:00:00)

- `middle` places the point in the middle of the group
(e.g. range 00:00:00 - 23:59:59 -> 12:00:00)

- `end` places the point at the end of the group
(e.g. range 00:00:00 - 23:59:59 -> 23:59:59)

name: series-dataGrouping-approximation
title: approximation
description:
The method of approximation inside a group. When for example 30 days
are grouped into one month, this determines what value should represent
the group. Possible values are "average", "averages", "open", "high",
"low", "close" and "sum". For OHLC and candlestick series the approximation
is "ohlc" by default, which finds the open, high, low and close values
within all the grouped data. For ranges, the approximation is "range",
which finds the low and high values. For multi-dimensional data,
like ranges and OHLC, "averages" will compute the average for each
dimension.

Custom aggregate methods can be added by assigning a callback function
as the approximation. This function takes a numeric array as the
argument and should return a single numeric value or `null`. Note
that the numeric array will never contain null values, only true
numbers. Instead, if null values are present in the raw data, the
numeric array will have an `.hasNulls` property set to `true`. For
single-value data sets the data is available in the first argument
of the callback function. For OHLC data sets, all the open values
are in the first argument, all high values in the second etc.

Since v4.2.7, grouping meta data is available in the approximation
callback from `this.dataGroupInfo`. It can be used to extract information
from the raw data.

Defaults to `average` for line-type series, `sum` for columns, `range`
for range series, `hlc` for HLC, and `ohlc` for OHLC and candlestick.

name: series-dataGrouping-dateTimeLabelFormats
title: dateTimeLabelFormats
description:
Datetime formats for the header of the tooltip in a stock chart.
The format can vary within a chart depending on the currently selected
time range and the current data grouping.

The default formats are:
```js
{
    millisecond: [
        '%A, %e %b, %H:%M:%S.%L', '%A, %e %b, %H:%M:%S.%L', '-%H:%M:%S.%L'
    ],
    second: ['%A, %e %b, %H:%M:%S', '%A, %e %b, %H:%M:%S', '-%H:%M:%S'],
    minute: ['%A, %e %b, %H:%M', '%A, %e %b, %H:%M', '-%H:%M'],
    hour: ['%A, %e %b, %H:%M', '%A, %e %b, %H:%M', '-%H:%M'],
    day: ['%A, %e %b %Y', '%A, %e %b', '-%A, %e %b %Y'],
    week: ['%v %A, %e %b %Y', '%A, %e %b', '-%A, %e %b %Y'],
    month: ['%B %Y', '%B', '-%B %Y'],
    year: ['%Y', '%Y', '-%Y']
}
```

For each of these array definitions, the first item is the format
used when the active time span is one unit. For instance, if the
current data applies to one week, the first item of the week array
is used. The second and third items are used when the active time
span is more than two units. For instance, if the current data applies
to two weeks, the second and third item of the week array are used,
 and applied to the start and end date of the time span.

name: series-dataGrouping-enabled
title: enabled
description: Enable or disable data grouping.

name: series-dataGrouping-firstAnchor
title: firstAnchor
description:
Specifies how the first grouped point is positioned on the xAxis.
If firstAnchor and/or lastAnchor are defined, then those options take
precedence over anchor for the first and/or last grouped points.
Available options:

-`start` places the point at the beginning of the group
(e.g. range 00:00:00 - 23:59:59 -> 00:00:00)

-`middle` places the point in the middle of the group
(e.g. range 00:00:00 - 23:59:59 -> 12:00:00)

-`end` places the point at the end of the group
(e.g. range 00:00:00 - 23:59:59 -> 23:59:59)

-`firstPoint` the first point in the group
(e.g. points at 00:13, 00:35, 00:59 -> 00:13)

-`lastPoint` the last point in the group
(e.g. points at 00:13, 00:35, 00:59 -> 00:59)

name: series-dataGrouping-forced
title: forced
description:
When data grouping is forced, it runs no matter how small the intervals
are. This can be handy for example when the sum should be calculated
for values appearing at random times within each hour.

name: series-dataGrouping-groupAll
title: groupAll
description:
By default only points within the visible range are grouped. Enabling this
option will force data grouping to calculate all grouped points for a given
dataset. That option prevents for example a column series from calculating
a grouped point partially. The effect is similar to
[Series.getExtremesFromAll](#plotOptions.series.getExtremesFromAll) but does
not affect yAxis extremes.

name: series-dataGrouping-groupPixelWidth
title: groupPixelWidth
description:
The approximate pixel width of each group. If for example a series
with 30 points is displayed over a 600 pixel wide plot area, no grouping
is performed. If however the series contains so many points that
the spacing is less than the groupPixelWidth, Highcharts will try
to group it into appropriate groups so that each is more or less
two pixels wide. If multiple series with different group pixel widths
are drawn on the same x axis, all series will take the greatest width.
For example, line series have 2px default group width, while column
series have 10px. If combined, both the line and the column will
have 10px by default.

name: series-dataGrouping-lastAnchor
title: lastAnchor
description:
Specifies how the last grouped point is positioned on the xAxis.
If firstAnchor and/or lastAnchor are defined, then those options take
precedence over anchor for the first and/or last grouped points.
Available options:

-`start` places the point at the beginning of the group
(e.g. range 00:00:00 - 23:59:59 -> 00:00:00)

-`middle` places the point in the middle of the group
(e.g. range 00:00:00 - 23:59:59 -> 12:00:00)

-`end` places the point at the end of the group
(e.g. range 00:00:00 - 23:59:59 -> 23:59:59)

-`firstPoint` the first point in the group
(e.g. points at 00:13, 00:35, 00:59 -> 00:13)

-`lastPoint` the last point in the group
(e.g. points at 00:13, 00:35, 00:59 -> 00:59)

name: series-dataGrouping-units
title: units
description:
An array determining what time intervals the data is allowed to be
grouped to. Each array item is an array where the first value is
the time unit and the second value another array of allowed multiples.

Defaults to:
```js
units: [[
    'millisecond', // unit name
    [1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, 100, 200, 500] // allowed multiples
], [
    'second',
    [1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30]
], [
    'minute',
    [1, 2, 5, 10, 15, 30]
], [
    'hour',
    [1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12]
], [
    'day',
    [1]
], [
    'week',
    [1]
], [
    'month',
    [1, 3, 6]
], [
    'year',
    null
]]
```

name: series-dataLabels
title: dataLabels
description:
Options for the series data labels, appearing next to each data point.

Since v6.2.0, multiple data labels can be applied to each single
point by defining them as an array of configs.

In styled mode, the data labels can be styled with the
`.highcharts-data-label-box` and `.highcharts-data-label` class names
([see example](https://www.highcharts.com/samples/highcharts/css/series-datalabels)).

name: series-dataLabels-align
title: align
description:
The alignment of the data label compared to the point. If `right`,
the right side of the label should be touching the point. For points
with an extent, like columns, the alignments also dictates how to
align it inside the box, as given with the
[inside](#plotOptions.column.dataLabels.inside) option. Can be one of
`left`, `center` or `right`.

name: series-dataLabels-alignTo
title: alignTo
description:
Alignment method for data labels. If set to `plotEdges`, the labels
are aligned within the plot area in the direction of the y-axis. So
in a regular column chart, the labels are aligned vertically
according to the `verticalAlign` setting. In a bar chart, which is
inverted, the labels are aligned horizontally according to the
`align` setting. Applies to cartesian series only.

name: series-dataLabels-allowOverlap
title: allowOverlap
description:
Whether to allow data labels to overlap. To make the labels less
sensitive for overlapping, the
[dataLabels.padding](#plotOptions.series.dataLabels.padding)
can be set to 0.

name: series-dataLabels-animation
title: animation
description:
Enable or disable the initial animation when a series is displayed
for the `dataLabels`. The animation can also be set as a
configuration object. Please note that this option only applies to
the initial animation.

For other animations, see [chart.animation](#chart.animation) and the
animation parameter under the API methods. The following properties
are supported:

- `defer`: The animation delay time in milliseconds.

name: series-dataLabels-animation-defer
title: defer
description:
The animation delay time in milliseconds. Set to `0` to render the
data labels immediately. As `undefined` inherits defer time from the
[series.animation.defer](#plotOptions.series.animation.defer).

name: series-dataLabels-backgroundColor
title: backgroundColor
description:
The background color or gradient for the data label. In addition to
regular colors, there are two special setting for this option:
- `auto` will set the background color the point's color.
- `contrast` will set it to a contrast against the text color, with
  an opacity allowing to see the underlying content. The contrast is
  great enough to ensure readability for the text according to
  accessibility standards.

name: series-dataLabels-borderColor
title: borderColor
description:
The border color for the data label. Setting it to `auto` will use
the point's color. Defaults to `undefined`.

name: series-dataLabels-borderRadius
title: borderRadius
description: The border radius in pixels for the data label.

name: series-dataLabels-borderWidth
title: borderWidth
description: The border width in pixels for the data label.
